title: Assignments
text:
The main idea is the lack of attention that statistical textbooks and software pay to graphics.
Three red flags:

It is wrong to assume that numeric calculations are correct and graphs are the “weird” part.
There is not one single way to analyze the data.
There is no virtue in just taking into account the calculus.

Given that:

Before every calculation, provide the scatterplot.
Plot the residuals against the adjusted (fitted) values after the regression.
Outlier — always investigate. Is it an error? Report it.
If the curves suggest non-linearity, consider transformations.




The default color was replaced with a custom sky-blue tone (skyblue).




In April 2014, Reuters published a graphic on the number of gun deaths in Florida, with the “Stand Your Ground” law (2005) as the turning point. However, the Y-axis was inverted, which conveyed a decrease in the numbers when the opposite was true. The numbers were not wrong — the form was. The solution is simple: keep the Y-axis in its conventional position.
Source: “How to Mislead With Charts” — Pacific Standard

title: Research
text:
Beyond the Bars: A Study of Recidivism Among Texas Inmates and the Influence of Sentence Length Master’s Thesis in Criminology, The University of Texas at Dallas, 2025 — Supervising Professor: Tony Love, PhD

This thesis examines the relationship between prison sentence length and the likelihood of rearrest or reincarceration among first-time inmates released from Texas state prisons. Using logistic regression, it finds that moderately long sentences (2–10 years) significantly increase recidivism, while very long sentences (25+ years) show no significant effect relative to shorter sentences — challenging deterrence theory and the presumed benefits of incapacitation.

Data-generating process. The data come from the Windham School District Biennial Evaluation project, an administrative dataset tracking first-time inmates released from Texas state prisons between September 2017 and May 2019 (N = 45,744). Records were compiled to evaluate the relationship between sentence length and reincarceration, with sentence length grouped into four bands and recidivism defined as rearrest or reincarceration within a set follow-up window.
